overview_raw: Delivery: in person. See details . A Marine Mechanical Technician is a person who installs, diagnoses, repairs and maintains engines, drive trains and other mechanical systems such as electrical, hydraulic and domestic fluid systems used in the recreational marine industry. This career involves all aspects of repairs to recreational and light commercial boats in regards to their diesel, gasoline, outboard engines, conventional inboard drive trains, stern drives, hydraulic and domestic fluid systems, and electronic management and controls. For more information Discover the answers to your burning questions by watching the video below, where a recent information session has been recorded: Marine Mechanical Technician Info Session October 2025 Next up Entrance Requirements
entrance_requirements_raw: Scheduled intakes February and September each year. Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first qualified basis as long as space remains. When available intakes are full, qualified applicants are wait-listed. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements prior to applying to this program. If you are uncertain or don't meet the requirements we strongly recommend you complete any applicable Trades Entry Assessments before applying. English language proficiency: one of the following: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent or BCIT English Trades Entry Assessment BCIT will accept your Grade 11 English final grade with proof of registration in English 12 for entry into the program. Math: one of the following: Foundations of Math and Pre-Calculus 10 (50%) or Workplace Math 10 (50%) or Other acceptable BC and Yukon courses or BCIT Math Trades Entry Assessment Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Recommended for success A driver's licence (Class N or 5) valid in BC is strongly recommended. International applicants This program is available to international applicants. Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the program. Please note that international students are not eligible to continue to an apprenticeship training program. To learn more about international student opportunities at BCIT, visit BCIT International . Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : While this program currently meets the eligible field of study requirement (CIP) to apply for a PGWP, this program is not eligible for a PGWP due to other criteria not being met. ( CIPC : 47.0616) Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. Program delivery In person: This program is delivered on campus. Program location Annacis Island Campus 1608 Cliveden Avenue Delta, British Columbia V3M 6M2 SkilledTradesBC BCIT transfers the student's name, contact information, Personal Education Number (PEN), and the name and date of the completed Foundation program to SkilledTradesBC. courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: In this course you will be introduced to the elements of safe working practices and will identify the common hazards and risks of accident/injury in a marine industry workplace. Here you will also learn about Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System (WHMIS), fire development and suppression, and the procedure and reasons to Lock Out equipment and the boat systems. This course will demonstrate to you to safe boat yard and marina practices. In portions of the course you will learn about proper lifting, blocking, and securing vessels and their equipment. Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

​In this course you will be introduced to the various tools and equipment and their use in the marine industry. This course also introduces you to the principles of steel and aluminum construction techniques and the principles of FRP construction techniques along with the selection of lubricants and additives. In portions of the course you will demonstrate the proper use of measuring, specialty tools, fasteners and fittings, shop equipment and the use of composites.​ Prerequisite(s): 70% in MMTF 1000

​In this course you will learn about safe operation of vessels and obtain a Pleasure Craft Operators Card (PCOC) approved by Transport Canada. This course also introduces you to the typical procedures for commissioning new boats and equipment, procedures for conducting sea trials, the common sources of technical data and the reasons for industrial standards. In addition, you will learn to read and comprehend the terminology, technical data, drawings, charts and graphs and write repair order descriptions related to the marine industry.​ Prerequisite(s): 70% in MMTF 1000

​In this course you will learn about cabin heating systems and the installation considerations. This course also introduces you to air conditioning theory, its components, and the refrigeration systems. In this course you will demonstrate the servicing of an Air Conditioning (AC), heating and refrigeration system.​ Prerequisite(s): 70% in MMTF 1000

courses.course_name: Fresh Water and Bilge Plumbing Systems
courses.course_overview_raw: ​In this course you will learn about thru-hull fittings, their materials and installation procedures. This course also introduces you to components and installation of fresh and waste water plumbing systems, water makers and bilge pump systems. In this course you will demonstrate the installation and servicing of vessel plumbing systems.​ Prerequisite(s): 70% in MMTF 1000

​In this course you will learn the characteristics of propane and safety considerations, regulatory codes and standards, and proper installation. This course also introduces you to davits, hoists and windlasses, fire suppression systems and electric and mechanical steering systems. In this course you will describe and demonstrate the safety considerations of propane fuel, precautions of installing and operating davits, hoists and windlasses, and the vessel fire suppression systems. ​ Prerequisite(s): 70% in MMTF 1000

​In this course you will learn the theory of hydraulic principles. You will also learn hydraulic system components as well as hydraulic safety. In addition, this course introduces you to hydraulic steering systems and components. In this course you will describe and demonstrate hydraulic system operation, install system components and diagnose hydraulic issues.​ Prerequisite(s): 70% in MMTF 1000

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​In this course you will learn about metals and their properties commonly used in the marine industry. You will demonstrate metal working operations, cutting, threading, bending and lay-out techniques. In this course you will learn to describe and service boat trailer components, and adjust weight distribution. In this course you will describe and demonstrate basic metalworking techniques with common marine metals.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

​In this course you will learn about welding safety, use of equipment and welding techniques, as they apply to the marine industry workplace. You will use welding equipment safely to perform basic torch operations.​ Prerequisite(s): 70% in MMTF 1000

​In this course you will learn about the principles of electrical theory, both alternating and direct current electricity and do electrical circuit calculations. In this course you will learn to read electrical schematics and use diagnostic and measuring equipment. In this course you will complete circuit calculations and use diagnostic meters and equipment. Prerequisite(s): 70% in MMTF 1000

​In this course you will learn and describe types of storage batteries and the different applications, how batteries are re-charged and serviced. In this course you will learn battery construction, applications and ratings. You will also learn how batteries are re-charged as per the battery's construction and the different ways batteries are re-charged. Prerequisite(s): 70% in MMTF 1000

​In this course you will learn DC electrical circuit components, installation techniques and standards. In this course you will learn about the engine starter, gauges and alarm circuits, their components and circuit requirements. This course you will also calculate, assemble and diagnose DC electrical circuits.​ Prerequisite(s): 70% in MMTF 1000

​In this course you will learn the function of self-contained Alternating Current (AC) generators and the criteria to be considered when installing a new system. You will learn to install a generator and how to diagnose generator faults.​ Prerequisite(s): 70% in MMTF 1000

​In this course you will learn the history, theory and operation of the basic 2 stroke and 4 stroke internal combustion engines. In this course you will learn spark and compression ignition engines and their operating principles. Also in this course you will perform routine inspections on various 2 and 4 stroke gasoline and diesel engines.​ Prerequisite(s): 70% in MMTF 1000

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​In this course you will learn about the support systems required for the engine to operate. These support systems include lubrication, cooling, fuel, intake air and exhaust systems. In this course you will learn the basics of drive system components, propellers, gear boxes and marine gears. In this course you will inspect, service and repair engine support systems and drive components.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

​In this course you will learn about the recreational marine industry which could include service and repair, parts supplies, sales and customer service. This course introduces you to the recreational marine service industry to gain knowledge about the working environment. In this course you will explore the marine industry by either job shadow, doing a research project or an assigned workshop project.​ Prerequisite(s): 70% in MMTF 1000

review_flags.raw: Option 3 requires three of ELEX 7010/7020/7030/7040 with an overall average of 70% or more.
Specialization Electives require at least 9.0 credits from the listed pool.
LIBS 7001 and LIBS 7002 are mandatory plus 6.0 credits in accordance with BCIT Liberal Studies policy.
After completing the prescribed course work, all degree program students are required to complete an industry-sponsored project in their selected area.
Two years relevant work experience is a graduation requirement, not an entrance requirement.
